text:
Predicates:
Timeless(x) ::: x is timeless.
DesignStyle(x, y) ::: x is a design style of y.
MassProductDesign(x) ::: x is a mass product design.
ZahaHadid(x) ::: x is Zaha Hadid.
KellyWearstler(x) ::: x is Kelly Wearstler.
Evocative(x) ::: x is evocative.
Dreamy(x) ::: x is dreamy.
DesignBy(x, y) ::: x is a design by y.
Max(x) ::: x is Max.
Design(x) ::: x is a design.
PublishedInYear(x, y) ::: x was published in year y.
Premises:
∀x (DesignStyles(ZahaHadid, x) → Timeless(x)) ::: All of Zaha Hadid's design styles are timeless.
¬∃x (MassProductDesign(x) ∧ Timeless(x)) ::: No mass product design is timeless.
DesignStyle(ZahaHadid, x) ∨ DesignStyle(KellyWearstler, x) ::: Either Zaha Hadid's design style or Kelly Wearstler's design style.
∀x (DesignStyle(KellyWearstler, x) → Evocative(x)) ::: All of Kelly Wearstler's design styles are evocative.
∀x (DesignStyle(KellyWearstler, x) → Dreamy(x)) ::: All of Kelly Wearstler's design styles are dreamy.
∀x (Timeless(x) ∧ DesignBy(Max, x) → (MassProductDesign(x) ∧ Evocative(x))) ::: If a design by Max is timeless, then it is a mass product design and evocative.
Conclusion:
∃x (DesignBy(Max, x) ∧ (Evocative(x) ∨ Dreamy(x))) ::: A design by Max is either evocative or dreamy.
